name: saT-TPOT
description: Abstract Background Team performance is critical in obstetric emergencies. The TeamSTEPPS™ Team Performance Observation Tool (T-TPOT) is widely used to assess team dynamics, but no version had been customised for obstetric simulation in Francophone settings. We aimed to adapt a French-language T-TPOT for obstetric simulation, establish its content validity, and conduct a preliminary rater-based evaluation of the resulting grid. Methods A prospective mixed-methods study was conducted in two phases. In Phase 1, a Delphi process was applied to a 33-item French-language adaptation of the T-TPOT by 16 invited experts from six Francophone countries (Belgium, Cameroon, Canada, France, Senegal and Switzerland). Three consensus rounds addressed the cross-context comprehension of the French phrasing, the necessity of each item (“absolutely necessary” for at least 50% of respondents), and its direct observability in a recorded obstetric simulation (at least 60% agreement among the twelve Round 2 respondents). In Phase 2, seven simulation experts, blinded to the instructors’ classification of two recorded postpartum-haemorrhage simulations (below versus at/above expectations), rated each independently using the final grid (1 = far below to 5 = far above expectations; 0 = not applicable); per-item rating distributions and discriminant capacity were analysed. Results Thirteen of the 16 invited panellists responded in Round 1 (81%) and 12 in Round 2 (92%).
